resources.string: Turn on your TV and check that your phone is on the same Wi-Fi network. Castor works with TVs that support DLNA (most Philips, Samsung, LG, Sony, Panasonic, Hisense…).
Add a TV by IP address
You’ll find it in the TV’s network settings.
The TV isn’t responding. Wait a few seconds before trying again.
The TV is waiting for the video, but %1$s isn’t sending it: Android has probably put it to sleep in the background. In its battery settings, choose “No restrictions”, then try again.
%1$s sends the video to the TV from your phone. If Android puts it to sleep in the background, the TV freezes as soon as you skip ahead.
%1$s relays the video to the TV. If Android puts it to sleep, playback stops when the screen turns off.
In its settings: Battery saver → “No restrictions”, and turn on “Autostart”.
In its settings: Battery → App launch → manage manually and allow running in background.
In its settings: Battery usage → allow background activity.
Turn the TV on and use the same Wi-Fi as the phone (not a guest network). Turn off any VPN. Still nothing? Add it by its IP address (Choose a TV → Add a TV by IP address).
The video freezes when I skip ahead

The app serving the video (often Stremio) was put to sleep by Android: let it run in the background (see the card in the Playing tab). With a torrent, the part you jump to must also be downloaded first: give it a few seconds.
The TV can’t read this format (often HEVC/x265, DTS sound or MKV on older TVs). Try another source or another quality.
Choose them in the Playing tab (Subtitles), or add a file. Many TVs ignore subtitles sent over the network: in that case, pick a version of the video with built-in subtitles.
The TV switches input at the end
Some TVs go back to the last input (HDMI) when a video ends or is stopped. That’s the TV’s own behavior; with Castor, prefer pausing.
Playback stops when the phone screen turns off
Let Castor run in the background.
Send any video to your TV
Castor spots the videos on the page
Direct link to a video or an .m3u8 stream
In your video app, choose “External player”, “Open with” or “Share”, then Castor.
Pick the one to send to the TV. If it doesn’t play, try the next one.
Find a video on the web
Open the page with the video and start playing it. A button will appear to send it to your TV.
Pick a video from the home screen, the browser or another app.
SRT, VTT and ASS files are supported. Some TVs don’t show subtitles sent this way.
Works with almost every TV. Skipping restarts the stream at the new position.
Sends the stream as is. Smoother skipping, if your TV can read HLS streams.
This video has its sound on a separate track, so direct mode is used to keep the sound.
Choose a TV to start playback.
Connect your phone to the same Wi-Fi as the TV.
This video is copy-protected (DRM) and can’t be sent to the TV.
The TV refused the request (%1$s). It may not support this video format.
The video site refused access (error %1$s). The link may have expired: reopen the page and try again.
Network problem. Check your Wi-Fi connection.
For streaming sites (HLS). Works with almost every TV.
Castor is free, with no ads and no tracking. Everything stays on your phone. Made with care by Rollando Studio.
